messages:
maya: adding customer report — streaming response truncated mid-JSON, final token cut off, finish_reason absent. request_id: req-0a1b2c, model: redwood-ggml-3b, mode: SSE.

linda: thanks. can you paste a minimal repro? browser + fetch or curl?

maya: customer sent this curl they used to reproduce:
```bash
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxx' -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-ggml-3b' \
  -d '{"prompt":"{...}","stream":true}'
```

maya: observed output ends with a partial JSON line like:
```text
data: {"id":"tok_...","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"...\n\n"}}    
```
(no closing ]} or data: [DONE])

sandeep: saw similar pattern in last week. hypothesis: edge (fastly/nginx) closing connection on idle chunk boundary, not flushing final chunk. can we get edge logs for req-0a1b2c?

alex (customer-bot): uploaded logs -> link: https://internal/logs/req-0a1b2c

jin: runtime logs show 'write failed: connection reset by peer' at 2026-03-12T18:02:11Z and then 'response stream ended without final frame'.

jin: can you repro with a local netcat to see if origin emits final 'data: [DONE]'? Maya, customer tried and origin did send it but it never reached client per tcpdump.

linda: interesting — tcpdump shows server FIN after final chunk but edge sent RST to client. suspect proxy timeout or buffer rules.

sandeep: confirm fastly had a 60s idle timeout + proxy_buffering off for streaming, but some intermediate nginx (customer infra) may have 'proxy_read_timeout' default 60s and then send reset. any evidence of long tail tokens? request had long completion time ~72s.

maya: customer says they get consistent truncation on long responses >65s, short ones fine.

jin: workaround we can recommend: enable keepalive and send periodic comment SSE heartbeats to keep connection active. e.g.:
```text
: heartbeat

```
we can push a runtime change to send a 1s comment if no token emitted >10s.

linda: repro steps we asked customer to run with node fetch to observe reconnect behaviour and idempotency:
```js
const res = await fetch(url, {headers:{Accept:'text/event-stream', Authorization:'Bearer sk-...'}});
res.body.on('data', chunk => console.log(chunk.toString()));
```
customer: they tried reconnect — on resume they saw duplicated tokens (no resume token support) so they got partial JSON + duplicate beginning.

sandeep: for short-term, recommend client-level dechunk+reconstruct: treat event-stream records, buffer until parseable JSON or timeout, then retry entire request with backfill prompt using last confirmed token text. not ideal but pragmatic.

jin: engineering plan: eng-runtime will add explicit final 'data: {"finish_reason":"stop"}' and always terminate with 'data: [DONE]' flushed as separate chunk. also add optional heartbeat config.

sandeep: infra plan: eng-sre to check fastly/nat gateway settings and add defensive config to convert FIN into proper end-of-stream and avoid RST on idle close.

linda: next steps:
- maya to send repro packet capture + curl output to eng
- sandeep to check fastly/edge configs + customer proxy notes
- jin to prototype heartbeat + final chonk flush
- ask customer to try node fetch with reconnect buffer and report

maya: assigned. I'll follow up in 24h. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy queued for eng-runtime branch heartbeat-proto -> staging at 2026-03-13T02:00:00Z

maya: thanks. closing interim ticket comms, will update when eng confirms root cause.
